findings.title: Native preparation retains two independent headers without retained admission
findings.trigger: Phase5 allocates activationState, then the independent activationSnapshot allocation or a later preparation step refuses/yields before adoption.
findings.cause: The two heap headers receive only OrdinalScanWork Reserve. Candidate/member admission and phase4 root metadata allowance do not cover these independent allocations. Both can survive a return in private preparation; successful outputs subsequently escape through DB state/snapshot publication.
findings.consequence: The claimed native retained union omits newly retained private storage. Refunding with the containing candidate would also be invalid after publication.
findings.correction: Remove private preborn headers and price their allocation/init before adoption, allocating and immediately publishing only in the nonyielding accepted original install under an explicit original-GC-output accounting decision; alternatively prove a genuine admitted lifetime for every escaped alias. Do not attach a containing-member refund to published headers.

findings.title: DB.Close proceeds with ordinary teardown after native join refuses settlement
findings.trigger: A genuine selected native physical I/O failure sets recoveryRequired while the original receipt, pending candidate and native dispatch remain linked; DB.Close is called.
findings.cause: JoinNativePublications returns the sticky error and Stop preserves active native dispatch, but DB.Close merely appends both errors. TakeRecoveryHandoff then accepts poison, captures/clears pending and transfers the original transaction to ordinary recovery custody; DB.rootPublication is cleared and later teardown runs.
findings.consequence: The native still-linked completion graph loses its required coordinator-owned pending/transaction state and DB discovery while its physical settlement is explicitly incomplete. This is not a valid successful Close and is not the selected error-state Close that preserves the same receipt/frame graph.
findings.correction: Make failed native join a real DB teardown boundary, preserving the original coordinator/receipt/transaction/callback graph and sticky error across repeated Close/Stop observation; do not invoke ordinary recovery transfer or resource teardown while native join is unsettled. Any alternate terminal handoff needs its own proved same-original representation.

findings.title: Native capture invokes ordinary owner-binding fan-out and synchronous unwind behind fixed work reservation
findings.trigger: Native capture phase4 constructs original stable pager operations while the metadata Owner has reader/enrollment bindings; success or a subsequent constructor refusal exercises owner growth/rollback.
findings.cause: Reserve6 precedes ordinary newStablePagerOwnedOperations. Its AddPending and NewOriginalCleanupCustody AddPending use ordinary resizeLocked, which visits all bindings and may roll back them. Failure invokes ordinary RemovePending and possibly custody.Complete synchronously. No actual binding discovery/forward/rollback work is admitted through the native work object.
findings.consequence: The actual pre-effect native Q32 route performs geometry-dependent synchronous work hidden behind a fixed six-record reservation, on successful construction and on unwind. The existence of a work-aware Owner growth seam elsewhere does not price this caller.
findings.correction: Make this SAME original constructor a native work-bearing continuation: admit protected discovery and real forward/rollback costs before effects, preserve partial custody and pending accounting on the original capture across refusal, and complete genuine refund after last aliases. Preserve ordinary nil-work behavior; do not substitute a larger fixed precharge or a helper owner/registry.
